summary: Kickoff for a 6-week POC to validate latency and cost tradeoffs for Lumos AI's customer-facing summarization pipeline. Agreed success criteria: p95 latency < 350ms for short summaries, cost per 1k tokens below target, and functional parity on 3 eval prompts. Timeline: access/setup week 1, baseline benchmarks week 2, optimization and mid-point review week 3-4, final exec readout in week 6.
topics: Access and infra checklist (VPC, IAM, sample data)
Timeline and milestones (kickoff, mid-point review, exec readout)
Risk/objections: data residency and SOC2/ISO requirements
transcript:
Header: 2026-10-21 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Sofia Patel, Diego Ramos (Redwood) — Maya Chen, Ravi Singh, Olivia Park (Lumos AI)

00:00 Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Sofia from Redwood, I can see Maya, Ravi, Olivia. quick intros?
00:08 Maya: hi, Maya here, head of ML at Lumos. we're building a realtime summarization feature for our analytics dashboards.
00:15 Ravi: Ravi, infra lead, I'll own the staging access and network bits.
00:19 Olivia: Olivia, PM, I'll coordinate success criteria and exec readout.
00:24 Diego: Diego from Redwood infra/SE. I'll run the benchmarks and help with performance tuning.
00:30 Sofia: Great. Objective today: align on success criteria, size the workload, agree benchmark plan, and land a timeline for the 6 week POC.
01:02 Maya: High level — we need to prove latency at scale and cost predictability. current baseline is a hosted model via another vendor, p95 around 420ms for ~150 token summaries, costs are a little high.
01:20 Diego: okay, and is the workload mostly short sequences? like 50-200 tokens?
01:26 Maya: yeah mostly 120 tokens on average, but there are spikes when users request longer context ~500 tokens.
02:00 Sofia: So suggested success criteria — p95 latency < 350ms for short summaries, p95 < 800ms for long ones, quality parity on 3 canonical prompts judged by your QA team, and unit cost target of <$X per 1k tokens — is that close?
02:22 Olivia: that's in the ballpark. we'll confirm the exact cost target, but yes.
02:30 Ravi: also need to confirm data residency and SOC2 details; we are regulated in EMEA so VPC and KMS are mandatory for production, but POC can be staging in our VPC.
02:48 Diego: Redwood supports private deployments and dedicated capacity; for POC we typically run in customer VPC with a lightweight footprint, or we can do hosted but with IP allowlist. for accurate latency numbers, customer VPC + dedicated instance is best.
03:12 Maya: sound good. timeline wise, how do you usually structure this?
03:18 Sofia: We propose week 1: access & dataset ingest; week 2: baseline runs (hosted/dedicated baseline); week 3-4: optimizations (batching, quantization, cache tuning); week 5: stability/rerun; week 6: exec readout. Mid-point review at end of week 3.
03:40 Olivia: that maps to our calendar; target exec readout the week of 2026-11-30.
04:00 Diego: For benchmarks, we'll collect token-level latency, p50/p95/p99, throughput (req/s), GPU utilization, and cost per token. we'll also run quality eval on your 3 canonical prompts and compute ROUGE/BERTScore.
04:25 Maya: can you also capture cold-starts and prefix cache behavior? our usage pattern has a lot of repeated prefixes.
04:32 Diego: yes, we'll instrument KV cache hit rates and show impact of prefix caching.
04:45 Sofia: Access checklist — Ravi you'll provide a staging VPC peering, temporary IAM user or role, and an SSH jumpbox for deployment. Also need sample dataset (5k queries) and a success criteria doc.
05:05 Ravi: We can do VPC peering and share IAM role; I'll get network team to open the ports. prefer to share a limited S3 bucket with sample data.
05:18 Olivia: we'll anonymize data first.
05:25 Maya: what about benchmarks for long tail — like 500 token summaries — we need those numbers too, and cost projections for 100k monthly active users.
05:36 Diego: we'll run scaled load tests and extrapolate unit economics. we'll also provide recommended quantization profiles — 4-bit if quality tolerates — and batching windows to hit latency targets.
06:00 Sofia: Risks/objections: data retention and compliance. we have SOC 2 docs and ISO attestation; we can share the security pack once SOW is signed.
06:15 Maya: good to see those. Also want a canary plan if we move to dedicated after POC.
06:25 Diego: we support canary rollouts and automatic fallback to hosted if dedicated cap is tight. we'll include runbook.
06:40 Olivia: ok, next steps?
06:45 Sofia: I'll send the SOW + pricing tiers by Monday 2026-10-25. Diego will share the benchmark runbook and sample scripts by Friday 2026-10-23. Maya will provide sample queries and success criteria doc by 2026-10-28. Ravi will provide staging VPC and IAM details by 2026-10-29. we'll lock mid-point review for week of 2026-11-16 and exec readout week of 2026-11-30.
07:12 Maya: sounds good. one Q: do you support customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest during POC?
07:20 Diego: for private deployments yes; for hosted we can support envelope encryption with customer KMS for staging datasets but production will need dedicated or private to fully satisfy KMS.
07:36 Ravi: that works.
07:40 Olivia: any ask from our execs? they'd like a short one-pager we can share ahead of the readout.
07:48 Sofia: We'll produce an interim one-pager before mid-point and a final slide deck for execs.
07:55 Maya: timeline and responsibilities looked reasonable.
08:00 Sofia: Great, thank you all. We'll follow up with the SOW and links. End of call.

Notes: transcript contains minor transcription errors and occasional speaker label overlap. References: benchmark runbook doc (will be shared), security pack link (upon SOW).
